slot.brief: Given three lanthanide ions (e.g., Ln3+ series), compute spin-only vs orbital contribution and pick which has the maximum magnetic moment — requires electron-counting in f orbitals and trend reasoning.

stem: For $\text{Ce}^{3+}$ ($Z=58$), $\text{Tb}^{3+}$ ($Z=65$) and $\text{Er}^{3+}$ ($Z=68$), what is the greatest spin-only magnetic moment? Use $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\ \text{BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

verdicts.working: Ce³⁺: 4f¹, n = 1; Tb³⁺: 4f⁸, n = 6; Er³⁺: 4f¹¹, n = 3. Their spin-only moments are √3, 4√3, and √15 BM, respectively. The greatest is 4√3 BM.

working:
$\text{Ln}^{3+}: 4f^{Z-57}$
$\text{Ce}^{3+}: 4f^1,\ n=1,\ \mu=\sqrt{3}\ \text{BM}$
$\text{Tb}^{3+}: 4f^8,\ n=6,\ \mu=\sqrt{48}=4\sqrt{3}\ \text{BM}$
$\text{Er}^{3+}: 4f^{11},\ n=3,\ \mu=\sqrt{15}\ \text{BM}$
$4\sqrt{3}>\sqrt{15}>\sqrt{3}$

Independent check: Ce³⁺: 4f¹, n = 1; Tb³⁺: 4f⁸, n = 6; Er³⁺: 4f¹¹, n = 3. Their spin-only moments are √3, 4√3, and √15 BM, respectively. The greatest is 4√3 BM.
solution:
For $\text{Ln}^{3+}$, the configuration is $4f^{Z-57}$. Thus $\text{Ce}^{3+}:4f^1$ ($n=1$), $\text{Tb}^{3+}:4f^8$ ($n=6$), and $\text{Er}^{3+}:4f^{11}$ ($n=3$).
Using $={n(n+2)}$ BM, their moments are $3$, ${48}=43$, and ${15}$ BM, respectively; the greatest is $43$ BM.
